prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
competitors_mentioned: Check the Missouri Department of Commerce
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” broker for everyone — the right one depends on whether you need an ACA/individual plan (with subsidies), short‑term coverage, major-medical with a particular carrier, your budget, and whether you want in‑person help. If you tell me your ZIP code and whether you need Marketplace (Obamacare) coverage, Medicare, or something else, I can find 3–4 well‑rated brokers or navigators near you.

How to find the best broker in Kansas City (practical steps)
- Decide what kind of coverage you need (individual/ACA, short‑term, dental/vision add‑ons, Medicare, etc.). Brokers often specialize.
- Prefer an independent agent/broker who represents multiple carriers (better chance to compare plans).
- Ask the broker these questions before committing:
  - Do you help people enroll in Marketplace (HealthCare.gov) plans and check for subsidy eligibility?
  - Which carriers do you represent?
  - Do you charge a broker fee or work on commission?
  - Will you provide year‑round help for billing/claims/renewals?
  - Can you provide references from other self‑employed clients?
- Verify credentials and complaints:
  - Check the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup (and Kansas Insurance Department if you’re on the Kansas side) to confirm the agent is licensed and see any disciplinary history.
  - Read Google/Yelp/BBB reviews.
- Use trusted tools to compare options:
  - HealthCare.gov “Find Local Help” (for Marketplace/Navigator and certified application counselors who provide free in‑person help).
  - HealthSherpa and eHealth (online broker/comparison sites that work with Marketplace and private plans).
  - Policygenius (national broker that compares multiple carriers).

If you want in‑person, free help for ACA plans: use HealthCare.gov’s “Find Local Help” to locate certified navigators or counselors in Kansas City who will assist you at no cost and handle subsidy calculations.

If you give me:
- ZIP code, and
- whether you need ACA marketplace coverage, Medicare, or something else,
I’ll look up highly rated local brokers/navigators and give 3–4 specific options and how to contact them.
